By way of this First Appeal Against Order, the appellants assail the Award passed by the Court of learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-III, Shimla, H.P, in MACT Case No.
170 of 2019, titled Rekha Devi and others Vs. Sh. Mohan Dishta and others, decided on 22.04.2022,
in terms whereof learned Tribunal held the appellants i.e., the driver of the vehicle and the owner of the vehicle, liable to pay the Award amount in favour of the claimants.

sentences.text: 1Whether reporters of the local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

2. Brief facts necessary for the adjudication of this appeal are that a claim petition was filed by the claimants on the grounds that Lokender husband of claimant No.1, father of .
claimants No.2 and 3 and son of claimants No. 4 and 5, was traveling in a Bolero Camper Jeep,
bearing registration No. HP08A-1969 on 14.02.2019.
The vehicle was owned by Dula Ram and was being driven by Mohan Dishta.
At around 10:30 pm, the vehicle met with an accident on the fateful night, within the jurisdiction of Police Station Chopal.
As a result of the accident, Lokender sustained injuries and he succumbed thereto.
As per the claimants, Lokender was on his way to purchase agricultural implements and had hired the vehicle for this purpose.
An FIR was registered on the occurrence of the incident, under Section 279, 337, 304A of the India Penal Code, against the driver of the vehicle.
According to the claimants, the deceased was 8th pass.
He was 28 years old.

He was doing the job of a casual labourer and was earning more than Rs.
15,000/- and in addition he was looking after the orchard of his parents and monthly income of the deceased was

around Rs.
25,000/-.

sentences.text:
The claim petition was resisted by the present appellants i.e. the driver and the owner of the vehicle, inter alia, on the ground that vehicle was not being driven in a rash and .
negligent manner but the accident occurred on account of heavy snow fall and a mechanical fault in the vehicle.
As per the driver he himself remained in the hospital for about 30 days on account of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
He was possessing a valid and effective driving license on the day when the accident took place and the vehicle was also duly insured.

He was in a semi-conscious stage after the accident and local residents who reached the site of the accident,
lifted him as well as deceased initially to the road side and from there to the hospital in issue.

It was further the case of the driver that he was administered local liquor at the behest of persons who rescued him, so that he could get some relief from his pain for the time being till he reaches the hospital.
4. The Insurance Company resisted the claim petition, inter alia, on the ground that the vehicle was being driven in violation of the conditions of the insurance policy.

It was also the case of the Insurance Company that the vehicle was a light goods vehicle and Lokender was a gratuitous passenger and in this view of the matter, said risk was not covered under the policy.

It was also the case of the Insurance Company that the .
deceased was not travelling for the purpose of purchase of agricultural implements nor he had hired the vehicle for the said purpose and, therefore, he was a gratuitous passenger.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, learned Tribunal framed the following issues:-
"(1) Whether Sh. Lokender died on account of rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. HP-08A- 1969 (Bolero Campar) by respondent No.1, as alleged?

OPP.
(2) If issue No.1 is proved in affirmative, whether petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
(3) Whether the petition is not maintainable, as alleged?

OPRs. 
(4) Whether the vehicle was being driven in violation to term and conditions of insurance policy as well as Motor Vehicles Act, as alleged? OPR-3.
(5) Whether the deceased was travelling in the vehicle as gratuitous passenger, as alleged? OPR-3.
(6) Whether vehicle in question was being plied without valid permit and fitness certificate, as alleged? OPR-3.

(8) Whether the claim petition has been filed in collusion of respondents No. 1 & 2?

(9) Relief."

6. On the basis of the evidence, which was led by the parties in support of their respective contentions, the issues were decided as under:-
 "Issue No. 1 : Yes.
 Issue No. 2 : Yes as per operative part of the  award.
Issue No. 3 : No.
Issue No. 4 : Yes.
Issue No. 5 : Yes.
Issue No. 6 : Yes.
Issue No. 7 : No.
Issue No. 8 : No.

Relief : Petition partly allowed as per  operative part of the award"
7.

While deciding issue No.5, learned Tribunal held that though it was the contention of the claimants that at the time when the accident took place, Lokender was traveling therein as he had hired the vehicle for transporting the agricultural equipment, which he intended to purchase but this contention went unproved on record.

Learned Tribunal held that though this stand was accepted by the driver and the owner of the vehicle but there was no evidence on record that the deceased was going for the purchase of the agricultural equipment and what kind of agricultural equipment was being .
purchased by the him.
Learned Tribunal also held that the claimants had also not proved the factum of the hiring of the vehicle for the said purpose.

Learned Tribunal also observed that the wife of the deceased had not deposed anything specific as to from where her husband was going to purchase the Mohan Dishta And Another vs Rekha Devi And Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18471419/
3 agricultural equipment and to the contrary in her cross- examination she admitted that her husband usually traveled on many occasions with the driver of the ill fated vehicle Mohan Dishta in the ill fated vehicle and that she had no knowledge as to whether any luggage etc. was loaded in the vehicle at the time of accident or not.

sentences.text: Learned Tribunal also took note of the statement of owner of the vehicle Dula Ram, who deposed in the Court that the vehicle was owned by him and Lokender was travelling in his vehicle as deceased had to purchase agricultural equipment but who in his cross-examination stated that when the accident took place he was not present at the spot and no record was produced by him to prove that the vehicle was hired by the Lokender on the date of accident.

Learned Tribunal also held that the evidence on record proved that driver Mohan Dishta and deceased Lokender were cousin .
brothers and they usually used to travel in the vehicle together.

Learned Tribunal also observed that the driver had admitted that record of hiring of the vehicle was maintained by his father Dula Ram but no record to the effeect that Lokender had hired the vehicle was produced before the Court.

Learned Tribunal also observed that the owner and the driver of the vehicle were given ample opportunity to prove the payment of any consideration for the hiring of the vehicle but they failed to do so and thus no cogent was placed on record that Lokender had hired the vehicle in question and he was going to purchase agricultural equipment.

Learned Tribunal also held while deciding issue No.6 that there was nothing on record to prove that there was valid permit and fitness certificate of the vehicle in question at the time of accident and whereas the accident had taken place on 14.02.2019, Mark A which was a copy of R.C. demonstrated that the vehicle was having fitness certificate only upto 23.08.2017. Learned Tribunal also held that the vehicle was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy as well as M.V. Act.

Thereafter, learned Tribunal while allowing the claim petition .
held that it were the driver and owner of the vehicle who were liable to indemnify the claimants.
8. Feeling aggrieved, driver and owner of the vehicle, filed this appeal.
9. I have heard learned Counsel for the parties at length and also gone through the Award under challenge as well as the record of the case.
10. It is relevant to mention at this stage itself that the driver of the vehicle happens to be the son of the owner of the vehicle.
The thrust of the arguments of learned Counsel for the appellants was that the findings returned by the learned Tribunal that deceased was a gratuitous passenger, are incorrect findings.

She argued that as it was the contention of the claimants that the vehicle was hired by Lokender for the purpose of transporting agricultural equipment which he intended to purchase and as this fact was admitted by the owner of the vehicle and the driver of the vehicle,
therefore, these being admitted facts, learned Tribunal erred in not accepting that.

She submitted Mohan Dishta And Another vs Rekha Devi And Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18471419/
4

sentences.text: that the fastening of the liability upon the present appellants was not sustainable in law and, .

therefore, the appeal be allowed and the Award be modified by directing the Insurance Company to indemnify the claimants.
11.
On the other hand, learned Counsel for the Insurance Company opposed the contention of the appellants.
He argued that the Tribunal on the basis of appreciation of the evidence on record, held and rightly so that Lokender was a gratuitous passenger.

He argued that there was not even an iota of evidence on record to substantiate the concocted story of the parties that the vehicle was hired by Lokender for the purpose of the transportation of the agricultural equipment.

He further argued that the accident took place during night hours and there was no occasion for the deceased to be travelling to a market for the purchase of agricultural equipment at such odd hours, more so, when the weather was also not good.

He submitted that all this suggested that the accident had taken place on account of the rash and negligent driving of the driver, who was drunk and Lokender who unfortunately was a gratuitous passenger in the vehicle died in the same.
He prayed that as there is no merit in the appeal, the same be dismissed.

12. Learned Counsel for the claimants were also heard .
in the matter and they prayed that appropriate be passed.

13. After careful consideration of the material on record, this Court is of the considered view that the findings returned by the learned Tribunal that deceased Lokender was a gratuitous passenger, call for no interference.

A perusal of the record demonstrates that except the bald contentions of the claimants, which was accepted by the owner and the driver of the vehicle that vehicle was hired by Lokender to transport agricultural equipment, no evidence was produced by the parties to prove this fact.
Incidentally, the claimants are appellants herein, are related to each other.
The claimants did not examine any shop owner from where the agricultural equipment was to be purchased by the deceased.

No evidence was placed on record either by the claimants or the appellants that the vehicle was hired and consideration was paid by Lokender for the hiring of the said vehicle, more so,
in the teeth of the fact that the driver of the vehicle had stated in the Court that record of the hiring of the vehicle was maintained by the owner of the vehicle, who incidentally was his father.

Another important aspect of the matter is that it has come on record that Lokender was a .
frequent traveller with Mohan Dishta in the vehicle in issue and that they were also related to each other.

In these circumstances, the occurrence of the accident in the late hours of the day, in inclement weather, wherein the driver was found in the influence of liquor is suggestive of the fact that in the absence of their being any material on record to prove that the vehicle was hired by Lokender to transport agricultural equipment, that he was just a gratuitous passenger, travelling in the ill fated vehicle at the time of the unfortunate accident.

sentences.text: Therefore, as the findings returned to the effect that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger, are correct findings which are duly corroborated from the evidence on record and on the other hand as there is nothing on record, from which it can be inferred that the vehicle indeed was hired by Lokender for transporting agricultural equipment, this Court does not finds any infirmity in the Award in issue and accordingly this appeal being devoid of any merit is dismissed.
Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, also stands disposed of.

(Ajay Mohan Goel) Judge .
